By connecting $BE$ and $CD$, and drawing the bisector $AN$ of $\angle CAD$, which intersects line segment $BE$ at point $M$ and line segment $CD$ at point $N$, what is the value of $\frac{AM}{AN}$?

Through point N, draw $NF\perp AC$ extending to intersect BP at point P, and $NH\perp AD$ intersecting at point H, and $NG\perp x$-axis intersecting at point G. Through point D, draw $DQ\perp x$-axis intersecting at point Q,\\
$\because$ $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\tan A=\frac{5}{12}$,\\
$\therefore$ let $BC=5k$, $AC=12k$, $AB=13k$,\\
By rotation, we can obtain: $AE=AC=12k$, $DE=BC=5k$, $AB=AD=13k$,\\
$\therefore$ $CQ=12k$, $DQ=7k$,\\
$\therefore$ $B(-5k,0)$, $E(12k,12k)$, $D(12k,7k)$,\\
$\because$ AN is the bisector of $\angle CAD$,\\
$\therefore$ $NF=NH$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle ANC}}{S_{\triangle AND}}=\frac{AC}{AD}=\frac{12k}{13k}=\frac{12}{13}$, hence $\frac{CN}{DN}=\frac{12}{13}$,\\
$\therefore$ $N(\frac{144k}{25},\frac{84k}{25})$,\\
Let the equation of line BE be $y=mx+n$,\\
Substitute $B(-5k,0)$, $E(12k,12k)$ into it: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}-5km+n=0 \\ 12km+n=12k\end{array}\right.$,\\
Solving them, we get: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}m=\frac{12}{17} \\ n=\frac{60k}{17}\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ $y=\frac{12}{17}x+\frac{60k}{17}$,\\
When $y=\frac{84k}{25}$, $\frac{12}{17}x+\frac{60k}{17}=\frac{84k}{25}$,\\
Solving for $x$: $x=-\frac{6k}{25}$,\\

$\because$ $NF\perp AC$, $\angle CAE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CFN=\angle CAE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE\parallel PN$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle MAE\sim \triangle MNP$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AM}{NM}=\frac{AE}{NP}=\frac{12k}{6k}=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AM}{AN}=\boxed{\frac{2}{3}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, and $\tan A=\frac{5}{12}$. After rotating $\triangle ABC$ $90^\circ$ counterclockwise around point $A$, we obtain $\triangle ADE$, where point $B$ falls on point $D$, and point $C$ falls on point $E$. By connecting $BE$ and $CD$, and drawing the bisector $AN$ of $\angle CAD$, which intersects line segment $BE$ at point $M$ and line segment $CD$ at point $N$, what is the value of $\frac{AM}{AN}$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let's establish a Cartesian coordinate system with point C as the origin. Through point N, draw $NF\perp AC$ extending to intersect BP at point P, and $NH\perp AD$ intersecting at point H, and $NG\perp x$-axis intersecting at point G. Through point D, draw $DQ\perp x$-axis intersecting at point Q,\\
$\because$ $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\tan A=\frac{5}{12}$,\\
$\therefore$ let $BC=5k$, $AC=12k$, $AB=13k$,\\
By rotation, we can obtain: $AE=AC=12k$, $DE=BC=5k$, $AB=AD=13k$,\\
$\therefore$ $CQ=12k$, $DQ=7k$,\\
$\therefore$ $B(-5k,0)$, $E(12k,12k)$, $D(12k,7k)$,\\
$\because$ AN is the bisector of $\angle CAD$,\\
$\therefore$ $NF=NH$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle ANC}}{S_{\triangle AND}}=\frac{AC}{AD}=\frac{12k}{13k}=\frac{12}{13}$, hence $\frac{CN}{DN}=\frac{12}{13}$,\\
$\therefore$ $N(\frac{144k}{25},\frac{84k}{25})$,\\
Let the equation of line BE be $y=mx+n$,\\
Substitute $B(-5k,0)$, $E(12k,12k)$ into it: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}-5km+n=0 \\ 12km+n=12k\end{array}\right.$,\\
Solving them, we get: $\left\{\begin{array}{l}m=\frac{12}{17} \\ n=\frac{60k}{17}\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ $y=\frac{12}{17}x+\frac{60k}{17}$,\\
When $y=\frac{84k}{25}$, $\frac{12}{17}x+\frac{60k}{17}=\frac{84k}{25}$,\\
Solving for $x$: $x=-\frac{6k}{25}$,\\
$\therefore$ $P(-\frac{6k}{25},\frac{84k}{25})$,\\
$\therefore$ $NP=\frac{144k}{25}-(-\frac{6k}{25})=6k$,\\
$\because$ $NF\perp AC$, $\angle CAE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CFN=\angle CAE=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE\parallel PN$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle MAE\sim \triangle MNP$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AM}{NM}=\frac{AE}{NP}=\frac{12k}{6k}=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AM}{AN}=\boxed{\frac{2}{3}}$.
